name: aigui_guide
title: How to write AIGUI blocks
description: Get the exact syntax for AIGUI blocks before writing any. Call with no arguments for the list of blocks, then with the names you will use. Blocks: chart, mermaid, katex, bigscreen, dashboard, scene, gravity, topology, molecule, graph, solid, function, optics, motion, physics, figure, quote, primitives, highlight, progress, citation. Each block is a fenced code block of JSON (or mermaid text, or $$ maths) inside ordinary markdown. The rules matter: most blocks take conditions, not results, and compute the numbers themselves.

blocks.description: Block names to get the syntax for, e.g. ["chart", "scene"]. Omit for the list.

locale.description: Language of the guidance. Default en.

name: aigui_render
title: Draw AIGUI blocks as PNG
description: Draw the AIGUI blocks in a markdown string as PNG images and return them. Draws: chart, mermaid, katex, bigscreen, dashboard, scene, gravity, topology, molecule, and markdown tables. Anything else in the markdown is ignored. Use it when a picture answers better than text — a chart of numbers, a diagram of a flow, a 3D shape, an orbit, a molecule. The images come back to you and are saved to disk; the result says whether they were also opened on the user's screen — if not, tell the user the paths. Call aigui_guide first for the syntax of any block you have not written in this session.

markdown.description: Markdown containing one or more AIGUI blocks.

data.description: Local data files by name, e.g. {"sales": "/abs/path/sales.csv"} (.csv, .tsv, .json). In a block's JSON, {"$data":"sales"} becomes its rows, {"$data":"sales","column":"revenue"} one column, {"$data":"sales","pick":["month","revenue"]} rows as arrays, {"$data":"sales","sum":"revenue"} a total (also count, max, min, avg). Use this whenever the numbers are in a file: the figures then come from the file, not from you retyping them.

width.description: Picture width in CSS pixels. Default 720; use ~1100 for a bigscreen.

name: aigui_open
title: Open AIGUI blocks in the browser
description: Write a markdown answer with AIGUI blocks to an HTML page and open it in the user's browser, where charts are interactive, 3D scenes and molecules can be turned, and walls and orbits animate. Draws every block: chart, mermaid, katex, bigscreen, dashboard, scene, gravity, topology, molecule, graph, solid, function, optics, motion, physics, figure, quote, primitives, highlight, progress, citation, plus maths, tables and code. Use it for a long answer that is mostly visual, for anything the user will want to explore, or for a [page only] block. Returns the file path. Call aigui_guide first for the syntax of any block you have not written in this session.

markdown.description: The whole answer: prose and AIGUI blocks.

data.description: Local data files by name, e.g. {"sales": "/abs/path/sales.csv"} (.csv, .tsv, .json). In a block's JSON, {"$data":"sales"} becomes its rows, {"$data":"sales","column":"revenue"} one column, {"$data":"sales","pick":["month","revenue"]} rows as arrays, {"$data":"sales","sum":"revenue"} a total (also count, max, min, avg). Use this whenever the numbers are in a file: the figures then come from the file, not from you retyping them.

locale.description: Language of the page's own buttons and labels. Default en; use the user's language when they ask for one.

name: aigui_edit
title: Change a page aigui_open wrote
description: Change part of a page written by aigui_open — a number, a panel, a step — without sending the whole answer again. Each edit replaces text in the page's markdown: find must be quoted exactly from what you wrote and occur once; include enough of the surrounding JSON to make it unique. The page is rewritten in place, opened again, and looked over like a new one. page defaults to the most recent one.

page.description: The page file path or name, or "last" (default).

edits.description: Find-and-replace edits on the page's markdown, applied in order.

title.description: A new title, if it should change.

locale.description: Change the language of the page's own buttons and labels.

name: aigui_topology
title: Draw a topology from real config
description: Read a docker-compose file, a Kubernetes manifest, or a directory of manifests and draw the system it describes as a topology — services, databases, queues, Services and Ingresses, volumes, and what connects to what — from the config itself rather than from memory. Opens it as a page and returns the ```topology block, which you can extend with steps (a request's path, a failover) and draw again with aigui_open.

path.description: Absolute path to a compose file, a manifest, or a directory of .yaml manifests.

open.description: Open it as a page (default true). false returns only the block.

name: aigui_export
title: Save a page as PNG or PDF
description: Save a page written by aigui_open as one full-length PNG, a PDF, a single self-contained HTML file that stays interactive, or a GIF / WebM of it playing — for sending or attaching. Returns the file path. page defaults to the most recent one.

page.description: The page file path or name, or "last" (default).

format.description: png (default) or pdf: drawn still. html: the page as one self-contained file that stays interactive — for sending to someone. gif or webm: one play of what moves on the page — a topology's or a scene's steps, a wall counting up — for a chat or a slide.

theme.description: Colour scheme to draw it in. Default light.
